prereg.question: which copilot's stated post-trade beta and most-correlated holding are closer to what the book then did

primary.metric: mean absolute error of beta after the trade
primary.test: exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank over per-origin mean differences

secondary: every other arm pair and target, reported, not tested for a headline
B2 hit rate of the most-correlated holding, bitget_daily and native_daily

bitget_snapshot.source: Bitget public v2 mix history-candles, USDT-FUTURES, 1H, MARKET

verdict: NO SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCE on the primary: mean absolute beta error 0.241 (ARGUS) vs 0.3603 (weekend-copilot, QQQ), ARGUS better on 7/9 origins, Wilcoxon p=0.0977
limitations: nine origins over one eleven-month period (December 2025 to August 2026); the primary test has little power, and p = 0.0977 does not clear 0.05
ARGUS is not significantly better than calling every beta 1.0: 0.241 against 0.2979, better on 7/9 origins, p = 0.2031

the open-session beta is not measurably better than the blended one at forecasting the next month's beta (0.241 against 0.2472, p = 0.8203); the module's claim that the blended figure misleads is about what the book does while the anchor market prices it, and is not supported as a forecasting advantage
books are random long-only weights over seven names; no short books, no crypto legs
not_compared: weekend-copilot's Friday-to-Monday gap stress (per proposed name, not per book)
its hedge comparator: a sizing choice for the proposed trade, not a hedge instrument
sector weights and HHI: the same arithmetic in both products
